name: My Env
description: Cross-platform environment variables and secret manager: safely inject credentials into cloud sandboxes, containers and local commands without chat leakage.
whenToUse: Look up, manage or inject environment variables and credentials into sandboxes, containers or local commands without exposing plaintext in chat.

items.name: guide
items.description: How My Env stores, masks, injects and exports values

tools.name: env_list
tools.description: List stored variables with masked values, memo and updatedAt; returns { total, returned, offset, limit, hasMore, items }. Sensitive entries are always fully masked here.

query.description: Optional keyword matched against key names or memos.

keys.description: Return only these exact keys (still masked); unknown keys are listed in 'missing'. Complements env_get for batch lookups.

limit.description: Page size 1-500, default 100. Use with offset for large stores.

offset.description: Number of matching entries to skip, default 0.

tools.name: env_get
tools.description: Return one variable's plaintext value; returns { key, value, memo, sensitive, updatedAt }. Call only when a command really needs the value, and never repeat it back into chat.

key.description: Variable key name, for example GITHUB_TOKEN.

allow_plaintext.description: Sensitive variables are refused by default, because the plaintext would land in the chat transcript. Set true only when a third-party interface hard-requires the raw value.

tools.name: env_set
tools.description: Create or update one variable; returns { key, message, maskedValue, sensitive, value_source }. Prefer value_from so the secret never travels through tool arguments; a plain 'value' is recorded in the chat transcript and the response says so in 'warning'.

key.description: Variable key name; letters, digits and underscores only.

value.description: DEPRECATED for secrets: an inline value passes through the tool call and is persisted in the chat transcript. Use value_from, or have the user enter it in the settings page.

value_from.description: Preferred source for the value. { file: '/abs/path' } reads the first line-safe content of a local file (a trailing newline is trimmed); { env: 'NAME' } copies the worker process environment variable NAME. Exactly one of file/env.

file.description: Absolute path of a local file whose content becomes the value.

env.description: Name of an environment variable already visible to the plugin worker.

memo.description: Short note describing what this variable is for.

sensitive.description: Mark as sensitive so the list shows a full mask. Defaults to the existing flag, or true for a new key.

tools.name: env_delete
tools.description: Delete one variable; returns { key, deleted }.

key.description: Key name of the variable to delete.

tools.name: env_write_file
tools.description: Write explicitly selected variables to a file (dotenv, shell script, or JSON) without exposing plaintext values in chat. keys is required; the file is created 0600, never overwrites by default, refuses symlinks and paths outside the working directory.

target_path.description: Target file path to write (e.g. '.env' or '/var/minis/workspace/.env'); relative paths resolve against the working directory.

keys.description: REQUIRED list of variable keys to include. Unknown keys are reported in 'missing_keys'.

format.description: Output format: 'dotenv' (KEY="VAL"), 'shell' (export KEY="VAL"), or 'json'. Defaults to 'dotenv'.

overwrite.description: Whether to overwrite an existing file. Defaults to false.

file_mode.description: Octal file permissions on POSIX systems (e.g. '0600' for user read/write only). Defaults to '0600' and is applied at creation time. Ignored on Windows.

allow_outside_cwd.description: Allow writing outside the current working directory. Defaults to false.

tools.name: env_exec
tools.description: Execute a command with selected environment variables injected into the process environment, without exposing secrets in chat. Output is automatically sanitized to mask sensitive values; on timeout the process tree is killed and the partial output is returned with timedOut: true.

args.description: Command line arguments as an array of strings.

keys.description: List of variable keys to inject from my-env into the command's environment. Omit or leave empty to inject all stored variables.

cwd.description: Working directory for command execution. Defaults to current directory.

timeout_ms.description: Execution timeout in ms (1000-110000, default 30000). The host caps a single node request at 120000 ms, so 110000 is the supported maximum; use a background job for longer silent work.

shell.description: Run through the platform shell so $VAR / %VAR% expansion works. Default false (auto-enabled for .cmd/.bat on Windows). Implemented as an explicit '/bin/sh -c' or 'cmd.exe /d /s /c' wrapper, never Node's shell:true; arguments containing spaces are quoted, and you own quoting when using command_line.

command_line.description: Full command line executed through the shell; takes precedence over command+args. Prefer this when you need shell semantics: you own the quoting, so nothing is silently re-escaped.

stdin.description: Optional text piped to the child process stdin (for example 'git commit -F -' or feeding a CLI prompt).

tools.name: env_probe
tools.description: Probe stored credentials for validity without ever returning their plaintext. 'github' checks api.github.com/user (plus repo push permission when repo is given); 'http' sends one GET request to url. keys is required, response bodies are never echoed back, and private/loopback targets are refused unless allow_private is true.

keys.description: REQUIRED variable keys to probe (max 20). There is no implicit 'all sensitive keys' mode, because probing sends the credential to a target.

repo.description: GitHub only: owner/repo to additionally verify push permission.

url.description: HTTP only: target URL (http/https). Must resolve to a public address unless allow_private is true.

header.description: HTTP only: header name carrying the token, default Authorization.

header_template.description: HTTP only: header value template containing {token}, default 'Bearer {token}'.

ok_status.description: HTTP only: status codes treated as healthy, default [200].

allow_private.description: HTTP only: allow targeting loopback/private/link-local addresses (local dev servers). Defaults to false.

allowed_hosts.description: HTTP only: optional exact hostname allowlist; when set, url must match one of these hosts.
